findings.title: suspiciousInterpolation flags a correctly written reference
findings.detail: The pattern /\{\{[^{}]*\}\}/ also matches inside "${{ inputs.x }}", so a correct reference returns the "{{ ... }}" warning. Any caller that passes a whole value string instead of only its text segments gets a false warning. No scenario pins this down.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN suspiciousInterpolation is called on the string "${{ inputs.x }}" THEN it returns the message "\"{{ ... }}\" is not reference syntax; references are written ${{ ... }}".

findings.title: Node-level pre/post hooks given as a single object are not normalised
findings.detail: normalizeNode re-prints references only when a node's pre/post is an array. A single hook object, which U25 would refuse but which can reach canonicalJson, keeps its reference spacing. Two such documents that differ only in reference spacing therefore hash differently.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a node's pre or post field is a single hook object rather than an array THEN canonicalJson leaves the references in that hook's input and with fields unnormalised.

findings.title: maxDepth 0 refuses every container
findings.detail: resolveLimits accepts 0 as a non-negative integer. With maxDepth 0, any object or array root fails with FORMAT_TOO_DEEP, while a scalar root still passes. No scenario pins this down.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN parseFlowText is called with { maxDepth: 0 } on the JSON text {} THEN it returns FORMAT_TOO_DEEP.

findings.title: suspiciousInterpolation flags a correctly written reference
findings.detail: The pattern /\{\{[^{}]*\}\}/ also matches inside "${{ inputs.x }}", so a correct reference returns the "{{ ... }}" warning. Any caller that passes a whole value string instead of only its text segments gets a false warning. No scenario pins this down.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN suspiciousInterpolation is called on the string "${{ inputs.x }}" THEN it returns the message "\"{{ ... }}\" is not reference syntax; references are written ${{ ... }}".

findings.title: Node-level pre/post hooks given as a single object are not normalised
findings.detail: normalizeNode re-prints references only when a node's pre/post is an array. A single hook object, which U25 would refuse but which can reach canonicalJson, keeps its reference spacing. Two such documents that differ only in reference spacing therefore hash differently.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a node's pre or post field is a single hook object rather than an array THEN canonicalJson leaves the references in that hook's input and with fields unnormalised.

findings.title: maxDepth 0 refuses every container
findings.detail: resolveLimits accepts 0 as a non-negative integer. With maxDepth 0, any object or array root fails with FORMAT_TOO_DEEP, while a scalar root still passes. No scenario pins this down.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN parseFlowText is called with { maxDepth: 0 } on the JSON text {} THEN it returns FORMAT_TOO_DEEP.
